channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Los Fotógrafos 2027 · OBRA Collective
item.description: The fifth annual Los Fotógrafos exhibition at OBRA Collective Gallery in Charlotte, North Carolina — a photography-only group show for Latine/o/a/x photographers with ties to Latin America and Iberia. OBRA (Observe, Bridge, Respond, Art) is an interdisciplinary Latinx arts group founded in 2013 out of the Latin American Coalition and now a 501(c)(3) running classes, workshops, artist studios and a gallery on the ground floor of Charlotte's VAPA Center. The call is free to enter and open to Latine photographers based in Charlotte and the surrounding area, with original work in all styles of photography; AI-generated images are disqualified. One to ten pieces may be submitted, and the gallery will tell selected photographers how many of their pieces it can hang, with a 20-inch cap on width; the gallery takes a 20% commission, so price accordingly. Work must be delivered in person — the exhibition opens Saturday, January 9 and closes Saturday, February 6, 2027, and decisions go out by Monday, November 9, 2026. Two things to know before you apply. The organiser's Spanish text contradicts its English text in two places: it calls this the second annual rather than the fifth, and it dates artwork delivery to November 11-13 where the English says December 11-13, so confirm the drop-off window with the gallery. And OBRA's own website does not carry this call — its exhibitions page still shows 2024 shows — so the EntryThingy listing and the gallery's Instagram are where the current edition lives. The 2025 edition, themed Right Now, was covered by Enlace Latino NC and selected ten photographers; the organiser contact is photographer and community activist Héctor Vaca Cruz. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Enchanted Winter · Mountain Artists Guild
item.description: The Mountain Artists Guild's holiday juried show in Prescott, Arizona, on the theme of wintertime — snow-covered landscapes and quiet winter nights, frosted forests, glowing lights, winter wildlife, celestial skies, folklore and whimsical winter worlds, with the Guild explicitly saying work need not be Christmas-themed and that abstract readings of frost, ice and snowfall are welcome. Photography is one of the four judged categories in its own right ("all types of photography mediums"), alongside original paintings, three-dimensional objects and handcrafted jewellery, and the Guild's own media list names photography twice. Awards are placings rather than cash: Best of Show across all four categories, then 1st, 2nd and 3rd Place within Photography, plus honourable mentions. The call is open to members and non-members alike, with Arizona artists particularly encouraged; up to five works may be entered, the first three covered by the base fee and each further work charged separately ($10 members, $12 non-members). Accepted work also stays in the Guild's online Web Gallery for three months after the awards. Two practical bars: all artwork must be delivered in person on intake day, October 26, with no shipping permitted at all — only members who cannot make intake may ask the Gallery Manager to arrange something else, and every piece must be for sale, priced to absorb the Guild's commission (25% members, 40% non-members). Framed or gallery-wrapped work only, minimum 154 square inches and maximum 1,728 square inches including frame. The show runs October 28 to December 30, 2026; the juror had not been named when this was listed. — Deadline: October 17, 2026. Fee: $30 members / $45 non-members (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Art Crit Night — November 2026 · Oklahoma Visual Arts Coalition
item.description: A free, curator-led public critique run by the Oklahoma Visual Arts Coalition, the statewide service organisation for Oklahoma artists. Two Oklahoma visual artists are selected per edition to present their work in person at 1515 Lincoln Gallery in Oklahoma City, receive structured feedback from the guest curator, and take questions from an audience of artists, arts professionals and collectors. Selected artists receive a $100 stipend and the application is free. The November 12, 2026 edition is led by Alexa Goetzinger, an independent curator, grant writer and development consultant based in Oklahoma City, who curated ArtNow: Materials and Boundaries at Oklahoma Contemporary in 2026, co-curated the national print exchange Connect: Collect and its exhibition Print as Object for Oklahoma City University's Hulsey Gallery from 2019 to 2023, and was previously Associate Director of OVAC itself. Work is shown to the room by projector, so documentation quality matters and detail shots help; smaller physical works can sometimes be accommodated, performance must be submitted as video, and artists may ask for the critique to focus on a website, an artist statement or a residency application instead of a body of work. The application asks for an artist statement, a bio, a stated goal for the critique and artwork samples. No medium is enumerated — the call says only "Oklahoma visual artists" and nothing excludes photography, whose projected presentation the format suits; OVAC's Grants for Artists programme has funded photographers, but this programme publishes no roster that affirms it. Applications close October 11 and artists are notified October 20. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $100.

item.title: Small Art Show 2026 · Paseo Arts Association
item.description: The Paseo Arts Association's annual small-works juried exhibition, held in Gallery II of the Paseo Arts & Creativity Center in Oklahoma City's historic Paseo Arts District through November and December. The brief is deliberately collector-friendly: original work no larger than 15 inches in any direction including frame, priced between $25 and $199. Open to all mediums of visual art in two and three dimensions, and the PAA's own preparation guidance names photography directly — "photos printed on metal do not need wire, if the hanging hardware is provided" — while the association also runs a dedicated annual photography show, Paseo Photofest, and a photography studio at the PACC. Reproduction prints are not eligible. Awards are cash: one Best of Show at $150, two Merit Awards at $75 each, and four to six honourable mentions, announced by the juror at the opening reception during the Paseo Arts District's First Friday Gallery Walk on November 6. The 2026 juror is Erica Nkechi, Executive Director of Heart Studios. The flat fee covers up to three works and is $15 for PAA members, $20 for everyone else; membership starts at $40 a year. Two things to plan for: artwork must be dropped off in person in Oklahoma City on Saturday, October 31 and collected on Saturday, December 19, and all work must be for sale. The association's commission on this show is stated inconsistently on its own site — the entry form and the call page both say 30%, while the juried-shows overview page says 30% generally but 20% for the Small Art Show — so confirm the rate before pricing. Entries close October 5 and selections are announced October 10. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: $15 members / $20 non-members (up to 3 works). Prize: $150.

item.title: Dek Unu Magazine — February 2027 Issue
item.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online. Dek Unu Magazine publishes and promotes fine art photography exclusively, and all fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome — each feature pairs 11 images with per-image commentary and an in-depth interview, and there is no word limit on the artist's own account of the work. The jurors read the documents as well as the images, and the magazine says it looks for coherent, intentional art, straight to strange, alongside technical excellence. The submission window for the February issue runs December 1-20, 2026, with the magazine closed for jury from the 21st to the 1st of the following month; submissions are by a single email carrying 11 separately named images plus bio and project commentary, with no zips, Dropbox or shared folders accepted. Entrants must be at least 18, and submission is limited to artists not previously published by Dek Unu. Dek Unu charges no fee to submit and does not pay contributors; copyright in the images always remains with the artist, and the magazine takes only the right to publish and to promote the magazine and the artist. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Art + Science Competition 2026: States of Change · Lenscratch
item.description: Lenscratch's annual Art + Science Award, now in its 2026 edition under the theme States of Change. The brief asks for photography that examines transition, transformation and instability within lived experience — change that may be gradual or abrupt, visible or difficult to perceive, ranging from emotional shifts to environmental conditions — and invites artists to consider how photography can reveal states where boundaries are not fixed and conditions keep shifting. Lenscratch's own submissions page frames the wider competition as looking for new work made within the last five years that shows an intersection of art and science, with topics as broad as climate change, environmental challenges or artificial intelligence. Awards are $500 for first place, $300 for second and $200 for third, plus two honourable mentions. The jurors are Linda Alterwitz, the Las Vegas interdisciplinary artist whose work integrates scientific inquiry with photographic processes and whose project Injection Site showed at FORMAT in Derby, and Ben Hickey, Executive Director of the Center for Exploratory and Perceptual Arts in Buffalo and previously curator of exhibitions at the Hilliard Art Museum. Entry is via a Google Form; Lenscratch states no entry fee on either of its two pages for this award, and every Lenscratch call in this directory is free. Winners are published on Lenscratch, which has run a daily photographer feature since 2007 and carries an archive of past Art and Science winners. The deadline is October 9, 2026. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500 + $300 + $200.

item.title: 2027 Lighthouse Works Fellowship
item.description: A six-week fellowship on Fishers Island, New York, from an organisation devoted both to developing artists and to the year-round cultural life of the island. Fellows get a private bedroom in a three-storey Victorian house shared with the other fellows, all meals — Lighthouse Works staff cook and eat dinner with fellows most nights, and all dietary needs are accommodated — a private studio about a mile and a half from the house, flooded with light and facing the ocean, and $1,750 in stipends. There is a wood and metal fabrication shop and a kiln on site. The primary obligation is simply to pursue your work; the only two commitments are an Artist Talk and an Open Studio, which bookend the stay. The organisation runs three fellowship tracks — Visual Art, Fiction and Composer — and states that artists at any stage of their career are encouraged to apply, with artistic excellence the primary criterion for acceptance. It publishes no list of accepted media, so a photographer applies under Visual Art, but its own roster of past fellows settles the question: Genesis Baez, whose photographs the Museum of Modern Art has collected, Peng Ke, a RISD photography graduate and Magnum Foundation fellow, and Widline Cadet and Lachell Workman, both photography graduates, have all held fellowships here. Applicants must be at least 21 and must not be currently enrolled in a BFA or MFA programme; Lighthouse Works primarily considers US-based artists, though international artists with a demonstrated history of living and working in the United States are also invited, and collaboratives, duos and collectives are not accepted this cycle. Applications for the 2027 cycle are open September 1 to October 1, 2026 (11:59pm ET) through SlideRoom, with a $25 application fee — a limited number of waivers are granted first come, first served if you email before you submit. The visual-art work sample is up to ten files, and only the first five are read in the opening round. Selection panels — a jury of experts in each applicant's field — meet from mid-October through December, interviews are scheduled in early January and results go out in mid-January. The 2027 calendar runs five sessions between March 9 and November 30, 2027. This year's programme is supported in part by a grant from the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $25 (waivers available). Prize: $1,750 stipend + six-week residency.

item.title: 2027 Wildacres Residency
item.description: A one-week residency in a private cabin on a mountain in Little Switzerland, North Carolina, offered at no cost to the artist. Wildacres has run the programme since 1999 and hosts around seventy artists a year in three self-catering cabins a quarter-mile beyond the retreat entrance, in weekly sessions running Monday afternoon to Sunday morning from April through October. One cabin is fully ADA compliant; another has a loft so two people collaborating on a single project can apply together. There is no internet in the cabins and cellphones generally do not connect except in the main retreat building — the isolation is the point. Residents may eat in the dining room with other residents, guests and staff, or cook for themselves. A few two-week residencies are offered each year, applied for separately on the form and not guaranteed. Artists cover their own travel and supplies; partners, guests and pets are not permitted, since these are working retreats. The selection committee is made up of artists, writers, musicians, actors, scholars and former residents, who review applications by discipline, and the programme is open to all artistic disciplines. The application form's discipline picker is organised by form rather than medium — Writing (fiction, non-fiction, poetry, memoir), Visual Arts three-dimensional, Visual Arts two-dimensional, Performance Arts music and dance, and Other — so a photographer applies as two-dimensional visual arts; work samples are no more than ten images. Applications for the 2027 calendar year opened August 1 and close at midnight EST on October 15, 2026, with a $30 non-refundable processing fee paid separately by PayPal after the form is submitted. Past residents must wait two years before reapplying. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: One-week residency.

item.title: Grants for Artists · Oklahoma Visual Arts Coalition
item.description: The Oklahoma Visual Arts Coalition's standing grant programme for individual Oklahoma artists, free to apply and reviewed on a rolling schedule with the next deadline on October 15, 2026. Four grants run under one umbrella. Creative Projects awards up to $1,500 to help an artist make visual art for public presentation. Community/Artist Partnership awards up to $1,500 for artist-led community projects. Education Assistance awards up to $500 toward training and professional development. Professional Basics awards up to $500 toward the ordinary infrastructure of a practice. Creative Projects and Community/Artist Partnership are reviewed twice a year, in March and October; Education Assistance and Professional Basics three times, in January, March and October. The grants are open to artists working in visual-based mediums as well as to curators and art writers, and OVAC publishes a scoring matrix and a sample application for each category, so you can see exactly what a panel is looking at before you write. It also gives written feedback on every request, funded or not. Photographers are among the funded: three of the March 2026 grantees work in photography — Liz Cousins, a Tulsa portrait photographer, for Queer Tulsa; Nicol Ragland for The Legends of Black Rodeo; and Barbara Paradise Kelly for matting, framing and display pedestals. Applicants must be 21 or over and must have lived in Oklahoma for at least the twelve months before the deadline; artists currently enrolled in BFA or MFA programmes are not eligible, and you may attach your name to only one application per cycle. You do not need to be an OVAC member. Funded projects must happen after the award and within a year of receiving the funds. Expect notification within four weeks of the deadline. Applications go through Submittable. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $1,500.

item.title: The Meridian Award 2026 — Cycle II
item.description: An independent international award granting a $1,000 fully unrestricted cash prize to one contemporary artist working in any medium, founded in New York City and open to artists worldwide aged 18 and over, with no restriction on nationality, location, education or professional status. There is no theme; portfolios are judged on artistic merit, clarity of vision, coherence of the work presented and the strength of a distinct artistic perspective. Photography is named in the award's own discipline list alongside painting, drawing, digital art, sculpture, print-based media, textile-based media, performance, sound art, video art and interdisciplinary practice; short and feature-length films are the only stated exclusion. Each cycle selects one winner and two finalists, and all three are invited to record an online interview published on the award's website and Instagram — but only the winner receives the $1,000. Apply through the award's own site with a short bio, an artist statement, a work description and up to five files, images and video links combined, with a $25 non-refundable fee; a discounted early-bird rate opens each cycle and fee waivers are not offered. Collaborative teams may apply as one. Artists keep full copyright, and the award takes only promotional reproduction rights on selected work. One thing to weigh: the jurors are described as invited contemporary-art professionals but are not publicly named. The inaugural 2026 cycle went to Brooklyn sculptor Wen Liu, a 2026 AIM Fellow at the Bronx Museum with fellowships from Yaddo, MacDowell and Bogliasco, with painter Matt Bollinger and interdisciplinary artist Andrius Alvarez-Backus as finalists. Cycle II closes October 15, 2026 and the winner is announced in mid-November. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: see-zeen Issue 21 Open Call
item.description: The twenty-first issue of an independent online photography magazine run out of New York and Berlin, open to any kind of photographic expression — portrait, landscape, documentary, fashion, abstract and anything else — with no theme set and no entry fee. Anyone over 18, anywhere in the world, may submit a series of six to fifteen images; the magazine asks for a project statement of up to 300 words, a work description of up to 100 words, a short bio with an email address, and website and Instagram links if you have them. Images go in as single JPG files, 2500 pixels maximum on the longest side, 72dpi in sRGB, each filename carrying the photographer's name and project title. Images and text files go together into a Dropbox file request; the magazine asks you to press Upload in Dropbox and then Send on the form at see-zeen.com. Copyright always remains with the photographer; by submitting you agree that see-zeen may publish and distribute the images on its website, social media and other media in connection with its own brand, and that the editors may crop images and make curatorial decisions. Everything submitted is also considered for the magazine's Instagram. The editors say plainly that they are overwhelmed with submissions and cannot contact photographers whose work is not selected, so there is no notification date. The Issue 21 deadline is October 18, 2026. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Women United Art Magazine — Issue XV
item.description: The Autumn 2026 issue of an international quarterly print and digital magazine dedicated to women in the arts, distributed worldwide through Amazon. The call is open to all women artists regardless of age, experience, education, race, sexual orientation or location, and the magazine states its focus explicitly: painting, drawing, printmaking, photography, digital art, collage, fibre and textile art, sculpture and installation. Selected artists are featured in Issue XV in either the In The Spotlight or The Curator's Pick section — the editors decide the length — plus a social media feature and a complimentary digital copy; artists picked for In The Spotlight are contacted with further questions about their work and practice. Everyone who submits receives a complimentary digital copy, and artists not selected for this issue may submit to the following one free of charge. The entry fee is a self-assessed sliding scale with no proof asked for: €35 standard for artists with stable income, institutional support or grant funding, €25 reduced for early-career or freelance artists, the underemployed and those carrying unpaid care responsibilities, and €10 symbolic for students and artists facing economic or structural limitations. The magazine says the fees fund waivers for artists who need them. Prepare an artist bio and an artist statement of up to 300 words each and between two and four images at a minimum of 300 DPI, cropped and ready for print, each filename formatted NAME_TITLE_YEAR_DIMENSIONS_MEDIA. Entries close 15 October 2026, selected artists are announced 25 October 2026 and the issue publishes in late November 2026. Editor-in-Chief is Mona Lerch, who founded Women United ART MOVEMENT in 2021. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: €10–€35. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Deep Shadows: The 2026 Lenscratch Halloween Exhibition
item.description: Lenscratch's Halloween show — the site has been running one on and off since 2011 — a free online juried exhibition for images that step out of the everyday and into the uncanny. The site's framing is that Halloween and photography go together in their shared ability to suspend reality and put the strange centre stage, and it asks for one picture that interprets the magic and suspense of the season. Juror Douglas Breault will select fifty images for the exhibition. Entry is free and strictly one image per photographer, submitted through a Google Form with a caption formatted exactly as Lenscratch specifies — copyright symbol, your name, title, location, website, Instagram handle. Submissions close October 18, 2026. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Belgrade Photo Month — New Talents 2027
item.description: The ninth edition of the Belgrade Photo Month festival opens its New Talents call to a younger generation of photographers, free to enter and open to any nationality, professional or amateur, on one hard condition: you must have been born after 1 January 2002. The theme is REBORN — to be reborn is to enter a new state, suggesting change but also continuity — and the festival explicitly leaves the reading open, welcoming any photographic genre or artistic approach that works through people, places, memories, identities, communities, nature or society. Entries are one project of eight to fifteen photographs, titled and numbered in viewing order, at a maximum 1920 pixels on the long side, sent by email with an artist's statement, a short CV including your birth date, and a text about the proposal of no more than 3,000 characters in English. AI photographs are not accepted. Proposals submitted to previous editions cannot be resubmitted. The jury — Joan Alvado, Julio Pantoja, Shirin Abedi, Sigrid Debusschere and Vesna Latinović — picks three best proposals plus the best local Serbian proposal, then awards first, second and third place and a prize for the best local proposal; all four projects are shown in the New Talents 2027 exhibition during the festival in Belgrade. The festival does not publish what the prizes consist of. Copyright and all other author's rights stay with the photographer, who is credited in every official festival publication and in the exhibition; nominated and winning photographs join the Belgrade Photo Month collection, and entrants accept that the organisers and general sponsors may use submitted photographs to promote the festival. Submissions close 14 February 2027 at 23:30 Belgrade time, successful authors are notified 7 March 2027 and the exhibition opens 7 May 2027. — Deadline: February 14, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Ephemeral Beauty — 2027 Juried Art Exhibition · Kahilu Theatre
item.description: The annual juried exhibition of Kahilu Exhibits, the visual arts programme of Kahilu Theatre in Waimea on Hawaiʻi Island, built this cycle around flowers and the paradox that the most fleeting thing in nature is also the one most permanently woven into human civilisation. The guest juror is Andrzej Kramarz, Gallery Director of the East Hawaiʻi Cultural Center in Hilo, and the brief ranges deliberately wide — flowers as signals of fertile land and water, as the lotus of Buddhist thought, as the blood-born blooms of Greek myth, as the ʻōhiʻa and lehua of Hawaiian moʻolelo — inviting artists to work anywhere in that territory. No medium list is published for this show; the brief's own note on what is sought says all approaches are welcome and asks artists to respond to the flower “across any medium”, and Kahilu Exhibits' separate call for exhibition proposals names photography among the media it programmes. Open internationally to artists 18 and over. The fee is $25 for the first sample and $5 for each additional media sample; accepted work hangs in Kahilu's Simperman and Suli T. Go Galleries with an opening reception on Thursday, January 14, 2027, and artists pay shipping both ways (Kahilu asks for two-day shipping or Mokulele Airlines' Wikiwiki service to Waimea-Kohala Airport, and specifically not ground services). Sales split 60% to the artist, 40% to Kahilu, and Kahilu retains sales rights for 45 days after the exhibition closes; work does not have to be offered for sale. One caution worth knowing before you apply: the listing's own prose is part-recycled from the previous cycle — it calls the show the "2026 Juried Art Exhibition", gives an impossible run of "January 14, 2026 through February 28, 2027", and dates the submission deadline "Friday, December 12, 2025" with notifications "Monday, December 22, 2025", while the platform's machine deadline field, last edited 14 September 2026, closes entries on 7 December 2026. The 2027 dates in the shipping and reception block are all weekday-correct, the 2025 ones are weekday-correct for 2025, so the stale block is the December one. Apply by 7 December to be safe, and confirm with the gallery if you need the later date. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: $25 + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: WHEN NATURE CALLS: A Call for Nature Art · The Lab on Santa Fe
item.description: A selected group show at The Lab on Santa Fe, a gallery in Denver's Art District on Santa Fe with strong First Friday traffic, asking for nature work that looks past the postcard. The brief is unusually well written and unusually broad: landscapes, wildlife, plants, weather, water, geology, the human body in nature and the many ways we live with, depend on, alter and imagine the natural world, with observation and invention equally welcome. Nature here can be majestic or microscopic, peaceful or vicious, funny, sacred, invasive, decaying, returning or completely indifferent to us; the gallery says it is especially drawn to the things most people walk right past. All styles and mediums are welcome, from traditional landscape, botanical study and wildlife art to abstraction, surrealism, conceptual work and full experimentation. The gallery publishes no list of eligible or excluded media beyond that line, and nowhere calls the show juried or names a selector — it says only that acceptance is not guaranteed and that reviewing art costs it significant time and money — but it has run a dedicated international street photography exhibition in this same space, so lens-based work is in scope. Location eligibility is listed as national rather than Colorado-only, one or two works per artist, $34 to enter. All submitted work must be for sale and the split on sales is 58% to the artist, 42% to the gallery; the gallery states plainly that acceptance is not guaranteed and that fees are non-refundable. The exhibition runs April 2 to May 1, 2027. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $34. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 3rd Annual Printmaking Micro-Residency · The Cedars Union
item.description: A month-long printmaking micro-residency at The Cedars Union, a non-profit artist incubator in Dallas, free to apply and open to artists of any medium — the call says so explicitly, and adds that no prior printmaking experience is required. One artist is selected to work with Taylor Gibson, the organisation's manager of programming, to brainstorm, produce and curate a closed edition of twenty hand-pulled prints in the process of their choosing: relief, intaglio, screenprint or collagraph. The imagery and every technical decision — number of layers, colours, composition, paper, image size, embellishments — are the artist's, all materials are provided, and ownership of the image stays with the artist, with The Cedars Union retaining the right to use it for marketing and outreach. The edition becomes a thank-you gift for the organisation's major donors. The artist receives a $400 stipend, five prints from the finished edition and a print placed in The Cedars Union's permanent collection. Apply with a 200-word proposal for what you intend to produce and how your work would translate into printmaking, optionally with sketches, plus three to five examples of relevant work. Two conditions to weigh before applying: you must be a current Cedars Union member (Community or Cohort) both when you apply and during the residency, and Community Membership is $80 a month on a six-month commitment or $100 month to month, so the residency is realistically for artists already in or moving to Dallas; and you agree to be present for the entire project. Community Membership applications are accepted year round. Previous recipients were Victoria Brill and Bao Nghi Ngo. — Deadline: October 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $400 stipend.

item.title: You'll Covet Your Eye Out — Holiday Show · Covet Art Gallery
item.description: A holiday group exhibition at Covet Art Gallery, a storefront at 1922-A South Coast Highway in Oceanside, north of San Diego, open since 2023, built around a single constraint: every work must be priced at $500 or less. Size is explicitly irrelevant — a tiny treasure and a statement piece compete on the same terms — and the gallery is after work that is covetable, collectible and giftable, whether someone is buying for a person they love or for themselves. All mediums and styles are welcome, all career levels, and the call is open nationally and internationally. Work must be original and must be for sale; the sale price given at entry is final and sales split 50/50 with the gallery, while artists are also invited to list further work on the gallery's own online marketplace, where the split is 70% to the artist. Artists retain full copyright and cover delivery both ways. Entry is $25 plus $5 for each additional image, up to twenty images. The show runs November 7 to December 12, 2026, with an opening party on November 7 from 5 to 9pm and a closing party on December 12. There is no cash award and no juror is named, though the gallery's own artist agreement calls this a Juried Group Exhibition — what is on offer is a selected place on the wall of a real gallery over the selling season. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $25 + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Non-Verbal Co-Learning Engagement — Spring 2027 · grunt gallery
item.description: A six-week paid engagement at grunt gallery in Vancouver for artists whose practice runs on gesture, text, signed languages or silence rather than speech. Two artists are selected and each receives $2,000 CAD, spendable entirely at their own discretion with no reporting to grunt; no completed artwork is required and no materials or artwork have to be handed over. The commitment is up to eight hours of co-learning: six weekly silent check-ins online, one interpreted or hybrid staff meeting, one silent accessibility committee meeting, a two-hour closed roundtable with other non-verbal artists, and a visit to a grunt exhibition, with travel and access supports paid by the gallery. One deliverable is required — taking part in an interview, video or other response that is archived and shared publicly, due March 5, 2027 — and artists also meet grunt's program director, curator and/or exhibition manager for feedback on presenting their work to galleries. Two hard gates: applicants must live in the Greater Vancouver Regional District, and must have a silent or non-verbal art practice. The gallery is blunt that working in a quiet visual medium is not itself such a practice — the program is about navigating professional arts spaces without relying on speech, whether by choice, necessity or circumstance — and that it expects a long-standing practice (participants have typically had four years of focused work; hobbyists are told it is not a match). Priority goes to artists who self-identify as Deaf, deaf, Hard of Hearing, Non-Verbal or Neurodiverse, to Trans and Queer artists adapting to silence through voice-changing transitions, and to Indigenous artists from the Host Nations (Musqueam, Squamish, Tsleil-Waututh). This is neither an exhibition nor a production residency and no maker or studio space is provided. No medium is named anywhere in the call, and grunt's own programme includes a lens-based photography residency, so photographers are not excluded — but the subject here is how you communicate, not what you shoot. Free to apply, by Google Form (a Google sign-in is required) or by emailing a plain-text or Microsoft Office application to aep@grunt.ca. Spring 2027 engagement runs February 2 – March 12, 2027, with a free ASL-interpreted info session on January 6, two days before the deadline. — Deadline: January 8, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,000 CAD.

item.title: Jazz Fest Volunteer Photographer Program 2027 · New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Foundation
item.description: The New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Foundation Archive selects photographers to document the 2027 New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival — the music, but also the food and art vendors, the cultural pavilion and the crowd — for permanent inclusion in the Foundation's historic collection. Selection is by a three-person blind jury of photographers scoring on artistic merit (60%) and experience photographing live cultural events or professional reliability (40%); no more than 150 applications are accepted. Photographers keep full ownership and copyright of their images, granting the Festival and Foundation permission to use them for non-commercial and educational purposes only, under a separate Terms of Agreement issued to those invited. Selected photographers are assigned one of the festival's two weekends (not both) and receive complimentary entry on assignment days, access to the Foundation hospitality lounge and free parking in designated lots, and may shoot the festival at leisure once the assignment is done. In return they must attend a compulsory photographers' meeting the day before the festival opens — that is where pit passes and tickets are issued — bring their own gear, deliver at least 18–24 photographs per act on their assigned stages with the selection left to the photographer, and be able to stand and walk long distances in heat, mud or dust. This is unpaid volunteer work: there is no fee to apply and no stipend — what comes back is credentialed access to a world-famous festival and a permanent place in a major cultural archive. Open internationally to student, amateur and professional photographers aged 18 or over; the application runs through CaFE and asks for six images, watermark-free. Two cautions about the Foundation's own page: the apply link in its How To Apply block points at a dead CaFE listing (ID 16128 — the live one is 18184, linked here under Submit via), and the same block dates the deadline November 13 while the page's own application-period header and CaFE both say November 14. Apply by November 13 to be safe. Festival dates are April 22–25 and April 29 – May 2, 2027. — Deadline: November 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Woodland Macro
item.description: Submit up to 5 images on the theme of woodland macro — close-up work made among trees, from fungi and bark to leaf detail and forest-floor life — for the 'One Thing This Month' reader competition (OP 334) in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). The winner receives a Lowepro Fastpack BP 450 AW IV backpack (RRP £139). The challenge is pegged to the main technique feature in that issue of the magazine, and entrants are asked to type the competition theme into the corresponding field on the submission form. Entries need captions of up to 75 words covering where, why and how each image was taken, plus full technical details in the magazine's stated order (camera and lens, focal length, ISO, shutter speed, aperture, tripod or handheld). Free to enter, uploaded in bulk through the magazine's Google Form, which requires a Google account because uploads run through Google Drive. The magazine publishes work taken outside in the landscape, wildlife, nature, adventure and travel genres — not fashion, wedding, field sports or interiors — and asks that images be made ethically and with sensitivity to environmental and conservation issues. Image manipulation is allowed but the magazine favours a gentle, sophisticated approach to editing. Entry is restricted to readers aged 18 or over, with one entry per person per competition, and the publisher's competition terms state that winners are notified by email within 30 days of the closing date and have 14 days to claim the prize. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Lowepro Fastpack BP 450 AW IV backpack (£139) + Publication.

item.title: Fridge Art Fair Miami 2026: Open Call for Artists
item.description: Fridge Art Fair returns to Miami Beach for Miami Art Week, December 1–6 2026, with “Gianni • Madonna • Coconuts”, which the fair describes as a citywide celebration of the Miami of the ’80s and ’90s, staged across three venues — the SoBe Visitor Center on Washington Ave, Uma House by Yurbban on James Ave and Habitat Hyett on Lincoln Road. Alongside the booth programme (booth fees start at $350–$500) the fair runs this open call, in which single works are submitted and assessed one at a time: “$35 for each work you submit … If your work is accepted, there is nothing more to pay. We take no commission on sales. You keep 100 percent of anything you sell.” The fair tells artists to “apply as many times as you like”, though the CaFE record itself caps an entrant at 20 applications, so 20 works is the real ceiling. Photography is named in the accepted-media list alongside painting, prints and drawing; work must be flat and wall-hung, no larger than 30 × 30 inches including the frame, projecting no more than 6 inches, under 35 pounds, wired and ready to hang. Sculpture and non-hanging work are considered case by case by email before applying. A jury reviews every work but no jurors are named, and there is no cash award — the return is the exhibition itself. One practical bar to weigh before entering: nothing can be shipped. Accepted artists, or a proxy, must drop off in person on November 29 or 30, attend their venue’s VIP opening night during fair week, and collect the work on December 7. Fridge does not insure artwork. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35 per work. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Artist Spotlight 2026 · Associated Artists of Winston-Salem
item.description: Once a year the Associated Artists of Winston-Salem takes over the Main Gallery of the Milton Rhodes Center for the Arts — the Arts Council campus building in downtown Winston-Salem — for what it calls a “highly competitive juried exhibit” of recent bodies of work by a small number of its members. The ask is a portfolio rather than single images: artists may submit up to 20 pieces of which roughly 5–8 are chosen, and the prospectus wants “a common thread that reveals an artist’s commitment to a theme, concept, or aesthetics”. Selection is by a panel of three to five jurors described only as “acclaimed local artists”; no names are published. Awards are $250, $125 and $75 for first, second and third place. Photographs are explicitly eligible — “Hand-pulled prints, original digital prints, and photographs are all acceptable” — while printed reproductions of paintings or drawings are not. Entry requires AAWS membership, which is bought online and is not itself juried ($75 a year Associate, $20 for students), and anyone featured in an Artist Spotlight in the past three years is barred. Results are posted to ShowSubmit accounts by the end of October 23. Work is dropped off on November 2 and collected on January 30, 2027; the show runs November 6, 2026 – January 30, 2027, opening with a free public reception on the 6th. Sales split 70/30 in the artist’s favour. — Deadline: October 19, 2026. Fee: $50 for 6 works ($5 each additional, up to 20). Prize: $250 + $125 + $75 + Exhibition.

item.title: Multiplicity · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on multiplicity — seriality, collections, classification, typologies, diptychs, grids and other unified arrangements. The gallery's framing: when subjects are gathered, compared or arranged, ordinary forms become evidence of pattern, difference, accumulation and order; a collection becomes a portrait, a typology reveals variation. Images may be found or constructed, documentary or conceptual, black and white or colour, traditional or experimental. The juror is Ross Anderson. Up to 74 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (21 November – 12 December 2026), featured on the gallery's online exhibition page and permanently archived online. Awards are a Juror's Choice (free entry into three future juried calls of the artist's choice), a Directors' Choice (two future calls) and eight honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, the printed exhibition catalogue and the online gallery. Entrants must be 18 or older, and images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's optional $37 printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing in its 22 × 22-inch black frames (mat openings up to 11 × 11, 10 × 15, 11.8 × 15 or 8 × 15 inches) and retains a 50% commission on any print sales. Notification is 28 October 2026. The org's calls page prints the deadline with a typo ('Cct 18'); its SmarterEntry portal reads 'Closes Oct 18'. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: 48th Annual Whitewater Valley Art Competition · Indiana University East
item.description: The 48th edition of Indiana University East's annual juried competition, staged in the campus's Tom Thomas Gallery in Richmond, Indiana. All visual art mediums except video and sound are allowed, and the eligibility text names photographs alongside paintings, drawings, printmaking, digital artworks, ceramics, jewelry, sculpture, textiles, installation and mixed media. Artists must be 18 or older and reside in the United States; work must be original and cannot have been shown in a previous Whitewater Valley Art Competition, and no piece may exceed 60 inches in any direction. The $35 registration fee covers up to three entries (three different views of each piece may be uploaded; entering more than three separate works disqualifies the artist) and is paid on IU East's own payment link rather than through CaFÉ, which carries no fee. Images are submitted via CaFÉ by 14 October 2026 at 11:59pm; the juried rounds are pre-recorded and shared on Facebook Live on 23 October with breaks for live audience questions, so that is when accepted work becomes known. Accepted pieces must reach the gallery by 6 November (hand delivery 3–6 November), the artist's reception and awards presentation is on 14 November, and the exhibition runs 14 November 2026 – 9 April 2027 in the Tom Thomas Gallery and Meijer Artway. Awards come to over $2,000 in total award money — $1,000 for 1st Place plus an invitation to a 2027 solo exhibition, $500 for 2nd, $250 for 3rd and three Honorable Mentions of $100 each, alongside a Chancellor's Choice Purchase Award whose winning piece enters the Indiana University East Public Art Collection. Nothing in the awards block narrows the pool by medium. Work is insured while on exhibition (not in transit); the artist covers shipping both ways with a prepaid return label. Note the gallery's own web page still shows the 47th edition — the 48th cycle's details are published on the CaFÉ record. — Deadline: October 14, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 entries). Prize: $2,000+ in awards + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Birds! · Museum of Northern California Art
item.description: The Museum of Northern California Art (monca) in Chico seeks original artworks for its annual bird-themed exhibition, staged during Chico's 2027 Snow Goose Festival — 'work must showcase birds, of all kinds, in all media'. All media are accepted; the museum bars giclée prints of original non-photographic art and states 'No AI please'. Entry is limited to artists residing in Northern California, defined as 41 named counties from Alameda, Butte and Humboldt to Sacramento, San Francisco, Santa Clara, Sonoma and Yuba. The entry fee is $15 for the first work and $10 for each additional, up to eight, non-refundable whether or not work is accepted; the museum's exhibition committee of professional artists and collectors makes the selection, with results emailed on or before 19 November 2026. Accepted work is delivered 17–20 December 2026 or 7–10 January 2027 (the artist pays shipping both ways), must be wired for the museum's cable-and-hook rail (no sawtooth hangers), must not have been shown at monca before, and stays for the whole run: the show opens 14 January 2027 with a reception on 29 January and closes 7 March 2027, though the entry agreement text still carries an earlier 10 January 2027 closing date. There is no cash award; the return is a museum group show. Entries opened on CaFÉ on 22 September 2026 and the museum's own calls page had not yet posted this call at the time of listing. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $15 (first entry) + $10 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Glassworks Magazine — Artwork Open Reading Period 2026
item.description: Free artwork submissions to Glassworks, the print literary magazine of Rowan University's Master of Arts in Writing programme in New Jersey. The magazine publishes still artwork — 'photography, paintings, collages, etc.' — bi-annually in its print issues, prefers to run several images by each artist selected, may add further images to its online galleries, and says it especially seeks to promote work by artists from marginalized communities. Submit five high-quality, print-ready images at 300 dpi or higher as JPG or PNG through Submittable. There is no submission fee: instead each genre carries a cap, and the artwork category closes as soon as 100 submissions are received or on 15 December 2026, whichever comes first, so early entry matters. One submission per genre per reading period; past contributors wait a full calendar year after publication before submitting again. AI-generated work is not accepted. Accepted contributors sign a contract granting exclusive first North American serial rights and first electronic publishing rights in English, with copyright reverting on publication; payment is one print copy of the issue, with a print-on-demand option for additional copies. The reading period opened 15 September 2026; the magazine's stated average response time is six months. Previously published work is not accepted, including work self-published online or on social media, and current Rowan University students, staff and faculty may not submit (alumni wait two years after graduating). — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print) + contributor copy.

item.title: Wildlife 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Printed photography exhibition on wildlife at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography, 4 to 28 February 2027 - a theme the gallery says has not had its own dedicated exhibition there before. The brief asks for "the visual delight of wildlife and the stories that they tell", in natural habitats or the unusual places animals turn up, and it also invites work on wildlife's relationships with humans, "both positive and negative", from the exotic to the domestic and the rural to the urban. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £50 participation fee (a discount is offered to anyone selected for both of the gallery's February exhibitions, this and Golden Hour 2027), which covers printing at 16x12, 18x12 or 12x12 inches in gallery-owned frames. Selected participants have their work printed and hung in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the website and included in an exhibition catalogue, receive a digital certificate of participation, have photos and video of the installed work shared on the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for its Photographer of the Month. Submit 1 to 8 JPEGs at 300ppi and at least 3,000 pixels on the shortest side, named Firstname-Surname, in one batch via Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox to the gallery's submissions address, stating which exhibition you are entering, your nationality or country of residence and any links. Deadline 9 October 2026; acceptance notification by 14 October (only selected photographers are notified) and payment due by 28 October. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Golden Hour 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Printed photography exhibition at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography, 4 to 28 February 2027, on the golden hour - the gallery's brief describes it as "the period of time in the day just after sunrise or just before sunset when an array of amazing colours can be captured", and asks for work that explores the world through the colour, light, shadow, texture and shape that light makes possible. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £50 participation fee (a discount is offered to anyone selected for both of the gallery's February exhibitions, this and Wildlife 2027), which covers printing at 16x12, 18x12 or 12x12 inches in gallery-owned frames. Selected participants have their work printed and hung in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the website and included in an exhibition catalogue, receive a digital certificate of participation, have photos and video of the installed work shared on the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for its Photographer of the Month. Submit 1 to 8 JPEGs at 300ppi and at least 3,000 pixels on the shortest side, named Firstname-Surname, in one batch via Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox to the gallery's submissions address, stating which exhibition you are entering, your nationality or country of residence and any links. Deadline 9 October 2026; acceptance notification by 14 October (only selected photographers are notified) and payment due by 28 October. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Myth, Folk & Superstition: Surreal Fables · Der Greif
item.description: Open call from Der Greif, the Munich non-profit for contemporary photography, for another edition of its Pulse online exhibitions, timed to launch on 31 October - "following on the heels of Halloween, just before Día de los Muertos and an upcoming Friday the 13th in November". The brief asks lens-based artists to explore modern folklore, cultural superstitions, myth-making and surrealism: from crossing paths with a black cat to honouring ancestors at vibrant altars, humans have always used stories, rituals and visual symbols to make sense of fate, luck and the unseen, and Der Greif wants photographic work that operates at the intersection of reality, fable and belief, whether staged cinematic storytelling, surreal dreamscapes or documentary studies of local legends, ancestral altars and talismanic objects. Selected artists are shown in an online exhibition in Der Greif's Pulse section, join an online roundtable critique with peers facilitated by Der Greif staff, and may be invited to submit a portfolio to Der Greif Studio, its route to artwork sales and commissions. Selection is on artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue and process, and engagement with themes of identity and community; the four staff jurors are named on the entry page. Submissions are one cohesive project not previously featured by Der Greif; the entry page and its upload form ask for at least 10 and up to 15 images, and the call's own conditions of participation agree, asking for “one project consisting of at least 10 images”. Der Greif describes the submission as free with a suggested €10 donation, but the Picter entry page charges a flat €10; artists who cannot contribute can email the organiser for a 50% or 100% discount code. Open to photographers and videographers internationally, particularly emerging and mid-career artists, with no age or regional restriction. Deadline 14 October 2026 at 11:59pm CET; results are due on 30 October. — Deadline: October 14, 2026. Fee: €10 (waivers available). Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Torn Boundaries · Bristol Art Museum
item.description: National juried call for collage from Bristol Art Museum, the nonprofit museum on Wardwell Street in Bristol, Rhode Island, for a show in its main galleries from 31 January to 1 April 2027. Torn Boundaries asks artists to explore the boundaries that define, separate, connect and sometimes divide us - physical or psychological, personal or cultural, geographic or political, historical or imagined - and the prospectus frames collage as the means: cutting, tearing, layering, juxtaposition, fragmentation and recombination that disrupt established relationships, asking what happens when an edge is crossed, a border redrawn, a familiar image removed from its context. This is a collage call, not a photography call: the prospectus names no media beyond collage and carries no photography clause either way, so photomontage and photo-collage fit its own definition of the form while a straight photograph does not. The juror is Francine Weiss, an artist, art advisor and museum professional with curatorial posts at the National Gallery of Art, Harvard Art Museums, deCordova, Fitchburg Art Museum, the Photographic Resource Center and Newport Art Museum, and a PhD in American art and the history of photography from Boston University. Cash awards are promised but the amounts are not yet published. Entry is open to US residents aged 18 or over; up to three works may be entered ($25 for one, $35 for two, $45 for three) as JPEGs under 4 MB, works no larger than 40 inches in either direction (diptychs and triptychs count as one), unframed work accepted with clips, magnets or an alternative hanging system, with a statement of up to 200 words. Accepted work must arrive by 15 January 2027 - the prospectus says by UPS in one line and by US Postal Service in another - or be hand-delivered on 14 or 15 January with a prepaid return label; the museum takes no commission and puts collectors directly in touch with the artist. Reception 7 February 2027. Entries close at midnight on Sunday 29 November 2026 through OnlineJuriedShows. — Deadline: November 29, 2026. Fee: $25 (1 entry), $35 (2), $45 (3). Prize: Museum exhibition + Cash awards (amounts not yet published).

item.title: AUTOPORTRAIT 2026: PLAY · Kuala Lumpur Photo Awards
item.description: Third interim edition of Kuala Lumpur Photo Awards' AUTOPORTRAIT open call, run this year with FORMAT International Photography Festival and taking FORMAT's 2027 festival theme, PLAY, as its brief. KLPA frames self-portraiture as always grounded in experimentation, trial and error and creative playfulness, and reads PLAY widely - fun, joyful, exploratory, experimental, deceitful, mischievous, subversive or rule-bending - from camera play and questioning the medium itself to documenting the act of play. Prizes are €1,000, €500 and €300, and the top 35 finalists have their portraits promoted online and screened at FORMAT27 in Derby, United Kingdom (11 March to 11 April 2027) and at future KLPA exhibitions in Kuala Lumpur. The jury is Jodi Kwok (curator at QUAD and FORMAT), Enrico Stefanelli (founder and artistic director of Photolux Festival, Lucca), D. M. Terblanche (South African self-taught artist, 2026 New Eyes Award recipient), Mari Katayama (Japanese artist whose self-portraits use her own body as sculpture and lens) and Sean Cham (artist, historian and RCA tutor). Open to professional and amateur photographers from all countries aged 16 or over on the deadline date; each submission takes up to 10 single images with captions, priced €12 for one, €24 for two, €45 for three to six and €65 for seven to ten, with a maximum of two submissions per photographer, and full-time students under 25 may enter one image free with proof of enrolment, judged alongside the main category. All photographs must have been taken between 2024 and 2026 (proof may be requested at verification), and entries are judged blind. The rules bar commercial or advertising images, heavily manipulated, HDR or content-altered work, and AI prompt-generated images in whole or in part. The call opens on 25 September 2026 - entry will be through the KLPA site's ENTER link or its Picter page, with payment by card via Picter - and closes at midnight Malaysian time (UTC+8) on Wednesday 25 November 2026, unless extended. Jury selection in early December, shortlist in mid-January 2027 and prizewinners announced in February 2027. — Deadline: November 25, 2026. Fee: €12 (1 image), €24 (2), €45 (3–6), €65 (7–10); students under 25 free for 1 image. Prize: €1,000 + €500 + €300 + Screening at FORMAT27 Derby (top 35).

item.title: International Photography Exhibition 168 (IPE 168) · Royal Photographic Society
item.description: The Royal Photographic Society's International Photography Exhibition has been held almost every year since 1854 and calls itself the world's longest-running contemporary photography exhibition; the 168th edition opened for entries on 15 September 2026 and closes at 23:59 GMT on Tuesday 15 December 2026, with an extra day to 16 December to finalise entries already started. Anyone of any age or level of practice, anywhere in the world, can enter, and RPS membership is not required. There is no theme and no categories: the T&Cs say there is no restriction on genre, process or technique, that film and digital, experimental and traditional processes are all eligible, that manipulation in software or the darkroom is allowed, and that found photographs may be incorporated - but work that includes generative AI in whole or in part is not eligible. Every entrant gets one free single-image entry; further entries, each of four images from one series or four single images, cost £35 (£27 for RPS members, £20 for under-30s), and multiple paid entries are allowed, with an early-bird prize draw for entries in by 19 October. The RPS longlists, a changing guest selection panel shortlists, and shortlisted photographers are then asked to send prints for a final anonymous selection of about 100 works, which the RPS mounts and frames at its own cost for a touring exhibition at partner venues; the RPS would not normally exhibit work larger than 50 x 60 cm. Awards are the £1,000 IPE Award and the £1,000 Under 30s Award (each with a year's RPS membership), a two-week solo exhibition at an RPS partner venue, four RPS Journal features chosen by the editor, five Selectors' Spotlight statements, and digital and social-media exposure for shortlisted work. Copyright stays with the photographer; the RPS takes a four-year promotional licence. The selection panel had not been named on the RPS site at the time of listing, and no notification date is published. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: Free (one single image); £35 per further entry (£27 RPS members, £20 under 30). Prize: £1,000 IPE Award + £1,000 Under 30s Award + Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: Lucky Star Issue 6: Womanhood & Femininity
item.description: Lucky Star is an independent photography magazine made in San Francisco by Madison Blanchard and sold through Green Apple Books and Beeks Books in the Bay Area and Waste Store in London. Its sixth issue is themed on womanhood and femininity: the call asks for projects about what it means to be a woman in society, women's empowerment, girlhood, female relationships, what femininity means and represents, how body and object contribute to those ideas, and social norms and the breaking of them, with the interpretation left entirely to the artist. Any medium of photo-based artwork is welcome, but it must be submitted as a series or body of work of at least five images, and ongoing projects are accepted. Only women, femme and female-identifying artists may submit to this issue; artists from anywhere and of any age are welcome. The deadline is Tuesday 13 October 2026 at 11:59pm Pacific. Entry is through a Google Form linked from the magazine's Submit page; the form requires a Google sign-in to open, so the fee, if any, could not be read - neither the magazine's site nor its own announcement mentions one, and the previous issue was free to enter. — Deadline: October 13, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: Publication.

item.title: River Margin — Spotlight: Ecologies
item.description: River Margin is a new ecology journal whose website runs a print issue alongside online segments; Spotlight: Ecologies is an annual online strand that highlights work on three named ecological topics, and for 2026 the three are Urban (Wild) Ecologies (wildness within the built environment - plants in cracks, neglected structures, material ecologies, repair and reuse, multispecies habitation), Nocturnal Ecologies (the worlds that become perceptible after dark - moths, bats, night-blooming plants, artificial light, bioluminescence, darkness and perception) and Arctic Ecologies (the flora, fauna, fungi and landscapes of Arctic and subarctic regions, from sea ice and permafrost to lichens and traditional ecological knowledge). Each topic takes photography and visual art (up to seven images by Google Drive link or email attachment, not WeTransfer) and writing (any form up to 10,000 words as one PDF). Submissions go to the journal's email address with the subject line for the chosen topic - 'SPOTLIGHT: Urban Ecologies Submission', 'SPOTLIGHT: Nocturnal Ecologies Submission' or 'SPOTLIGHT: Arctic Ecologies Submission' - by 1 October 2026, after which the strand launches online. There is no entry fee, artists retain full rights, no AI is accepted in any category, and only successful submissions receive a reply. This is the online segment; the journal's print Issue 1 (closing 1 November) is listed separately. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online publication.

item.title: Exhibition Proposals — Q4 2026 · Holter Museum of Art
item.description: The Holter Museum of Art in Helena, Montana mounts twenty to twenty-five solo and group exhibitions a year across three main galleries and two smaller ones, each running six weeks to three months, and fills part of that programme from artist proposals reviewed on a rolling quarterly basis. Four selection dates are set each year; the final 2026 round has a submission deadline of December 6 for a December 9 review, and it is the last chance before the 2027 cycle. Applicants hear back within two weeks of the selection date, but the museum organises exhibitions one to three years in advance, so a successful proposal is not a near-term show. Proposals are accepted from artists nationwide and internationally, and two or more artists may propose together. A proposal takes a cover letter giving the exhibition title, a description of the concept, content and medium, and the method of delivery; an artist statement, biography and CV; any educational programming or community outreach on offer; a budget and any special accommodations; an image list with titles, dimensions, years and media; and ten high-quality images, with up to twenty accepted, uploaded as individual files (PDF for everything else, no HEIC). The online form charges a $20 application fee on its second step. The museum shows photography as a matter of course - its Baucus Gallery solo this autumn, Jessica Hays's The Sun Sets Midafternoon, is by a Montana photographer working in pigment prints, artist books and historic photographic processes. — Deadline: December 6, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Here & Now · Bristol Art Museum
item.description: Bristol Art Museum, a nonprofit museum on Wardwell Street in Bristol, Rhode Island, closes its year-long recognition of America's 250th anniversary by turning from national history to the place it calls home. Here & Now is a regional juried exhibition of work inspired by Rhode Island, the greater Narragansett Bay area or the Southern New England region: the prospectus lists photography first among the media it brings together, alongside painting, printmaking, fiber, mixed media and other two- and three-dimensional work, and the subjects it suggests run from coastal landscapes, Bristol Harbor and working waterfronts to architecture, neighbourhoods, natural environments, community life and personal interpretations of place, whether representational or conceptual. The juror is Dan Wallace, a RISD-trained landscape architect with Sudbury Design Group since 1985. Selected works hang in the Livingston Gallery from December 6, 2026 to January 10, 2027, with a reception on December 6 from 2 to 4pm; the museum's other galleries show harbour photographs by featured Bristol artist Brendon Adams and new work from its 2026 Harbor Residency at the same time. Entry is open to artists in Rhode Island and the surrounding region who can hand-deliver accepted work on November 23 or 24 (no shipped work is accepted); work must have been completed in 2026, be no more than 40 inches in any direction (3D work under 50 lb), and up to three pieces may be entered - $15 for one, $25 for two, $35 for three - as JPEGs under 4 MB. The show is part of the museum's annual fundraising, and exhibiting artists agree to donate 50% of any sale to the museum. Entries close Sunday November 8, 2026 through OnlineJuriedShows. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: $15 (1 entry), $25 (2), $35 (3). Prize: Museum exhibition.

item.title: Where Stories Gather · WaterWorks Art Museum
item.description: The WaterWorks Art Museum sits on the banks of the Yellowstone River in Miles City, Montana, in a 1910 water plant listed on the National Register of Historic Places - its galleries are the renovated basins that produced the town's drinking water for sixty years - and it has run an annual juried show since at least 2014 (the 2018 edition was titled Photography Plus). The 2026-27 edition, Where Stories Gather, invites artists working in two- and three-dimensional media to explore the places, memories, objects, traditions and encounters where narratives take shape, from landscapes, homes and communities to personal histories, cultural symbols and quiet moments of reflection. The prospectus names no media list beyond 2D and 3D, so photographers should note that eligibility is unenumerated; the museum's own juried-show history includes a photography edition. The juror is Jenn Hall Tooke, a museum artist and paleontology-trained community advocate who has worked at WaterWorks and the Carter County Museum in Ekalaka. Six cash awards: $300 Best in Show, $200, $150 and $100 honourable mentions, a $150 Director's Choice and a $100 People's Choice. Entries are open to artists nationwide; work must be original, made within the last two years, at least 12 inches on one side and no more than 60 inches in any direction, and for sale (35% commission). A $40 fee covers up to three entries, judged from digital images, with results emailed by December 22; accepted work is due January 14, the show runs from the January 29, 2027 reception to March 18, and a committee picks about 25 pieces for a smaller collection that tours galleries in eastern Montana for the rest of 2027. Shipping both ways is at the artist's expense, and an artist who withdraws an accepted piece is barred from the museum's juried shows for three years. Deadline Wednesday December 16, 2026 through OnlineJuriedShows. — Deadline: December 16, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 3 entries). Prize: $300 Best in Show + Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Reflection Art Show · Paul Nigra Center for Creative Arts
item.description: The Paul Nigra Center for Creative Arts is a community arts centre in Gloversville, New York, run by The Arc Lexington, that mounts several open art shows a year (its Winter, Regional and New York State Summer shows draw 40 to 60 artists each, and it hosts an annual show of Adirondack Life magazine's photography contest winners). The 2026 Reflection Art Show invites artists everywhere to submit works of any medium and any subject - 'your best new art, or reflect on the past by showing off your favorite pieces from your portfolio' - to close out 2026 and welcome 2027. Up to three works cost $25 ($15 for centre members), with up to two more at $10 each ($7 for members). Work must be original and not previously shown at the centre, hanging pieces may not exceed 25 pounds, and content with nudity or sexual themes is not accepted because of the centre's family audience. Entries can be made through OnlineJuriedShows, through the centre's own Google Form, or by mailing or emailing the prospectus form. Selection notifications go out by October 7; accepted work must be delivered or shipped to arrive by October 24 (shipped work carries a $10 handling fee and needs a prepaid return label), and the show runs October 30, 2026 to January 7, 2027 with a public reception on November 5 from 4 to 7pm. Awards and prizes are funded by supporters and announced November 4, but the amounts are not published. The centre takes 20% on sales; work need not be for sale. Deadline October 4, 2026. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: $25 for up to 3 works ($15 members); $10 per additional work up to 5. Prize: Exhibition + Awards at reception.

item.title: Open Space: Art About the Land 2026 · Minnetrista Museum & Gardens
item.description: Since 2001 Open Space: Art About the Land has asked Indiana artists to draw creative inspiration from the land and celebrate the idea of open space. It is an annual juried competition and exhibition developed by Minnetrista Museum & Gardens in Muncie and the Anderson Museum of Art in partnership with Red-tail Land Conservancy, and the 2026 show hangs at both museums from November 7, 2026 to January 3, 2027, with a portion of proceeds going to the conservancy's habitat work. Any artist 18 or older who is a present or former resident of Indiana may enter up to three works made in the last three years for one $35 fee; eligible work is listed as ceramics, digital art, drawings, fiber, mixed media, paintings, prints, sculptures, metalwork and photography (digital work must be printed; video and audio are not eligible), it must address 'the spirit of open space with reference to the land', may not have been made as part of a class, and may not exceed 50 pounds; the two surfaces disagree on size - the org's prospectus PDF caps entries at 60 inches in any direction while the ShowSubmit entry page says 48 inches. The ShowSubmit entry page also states that no use of artificial intelligence, in the conception or development of the artwork, is permitted (the PDF carries no AI clause). The juror is India Cruse-Griffin, a Muncie-trained mixed-media collage artist and Harrison Center studio artist who won the Indy Arts Council's DeHaan Artist of Distinction in 2025. Awards total $1,500 at her discretion: $500, $350 and $250 for first to third place, $100 merit awards for photography, three-dimensional work and the Jim Faulkner landscape award, and the $100 Stefan and Joan Anderson Prize for the best piece representing a Red-tail nature preserve. Results are emailed October 2; accepted work is dropped off by appointment on October 16 or 17, the awards reception is November 6 at Minnetrista, and both venues take 30% on sales. Entries close at 11:59pm on Monday September 28, 2026 through ShowSubmit. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: $1,500 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: In Between Gallery Open Call 2026 · Fabrica
item.description: Fabrica is a contemporary art gallery in a Grade II-listed former church in Brighton's Lanes, founded as an artist-led space in 1996. Its In Between Gallery turns the gallery's picture window on Duke Street - one of the city's busiest pedestrianised streets, busy into the night - into a temporary photography gallery, and this ninth-year open call, run with Spectrum Photographic, Photo Fringe, Jane & Jeremy and POST, seeks one image by one UK-based photographer or artist group who considers themselves early to mid-career. The selected image is exhibited from November 2026 to April 2027 (with occasional short removals around venue hire), and the artist receives a £350 fee covering the exhibition, a talk at Fabrica's Photography Networking Event on Thursday 4 February 2027 (travel paid separately) and an Instagram takeover from 28 January to 4 February; the artist and image are also promoted by Fabrica and its partners. Practicalities that the panel weighs: the window is roughly 2.7 by 2.25 metres, so square formats sit well, and its light filter does not favour predominantly dark or black-and-white images. There is no theme and no entry fee, and the call is open to UK residents only. Applications go through a Google Form with up to three low-res images, a title and context document, a biography or CV, and a link to a website or Instagram; the deadline is 12 noon on Monday 26 October 2026 and the selected artist is told on Friday 30 October. — Deadline: October 26, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £350 + Exhibition.

item.title: Unfold — Fabrica x Sussex Contemporary Open Call 2027
item.description: Sussex Contemporary, an independent arts organisation that stages curated exhibitions and artist opportunities across South East England, and Fabrica, the contemporary art gallery in a Grade II-listed former church in Brighton's Lanes, follow their first partnership exhibition Resonance (2026) with Unfold, a UK-wide judged open call whose selected works are shown at Fabrica from 16 April to 9 May 2027. The theme - to reveal, develop or become; an idea taking shape, a landscape changing, a practice growing over time - is offered as a starting point rather than a constraint, and the organisers say they are as interested in process as in outcome and in the stories behind the work. Original work in any discipline is welcome, with photography named alongside drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, jewellery, illustration, mixed media, installation, moving image, sound and performance (giclée and other reproduction prints are refused as printmaking entries). Entry is open to amateur and professional artists with a UK connection - born, educated, living or working in the UK, or another clear link. Each work costs £20 to enter, up to three per artist, bought through the Sussex Contemporary shop, after which a closed artist page links the submission form; selection is by an independent five-person panel, announced through the call, of which the first named is Fabrica co-director Liz Whitehead, and is anonymous wherever possible. Two prizes follow selection without a separate application: the WeAreBrighton Prize (a year of the monthly WeAreBrighton talks plus mentoring with Sussex Contemporary founder Jo Myles) and Unfold in the Window, a further showing in Fabrica's Duke Street window gallery between May and September 2027. All selected work is for sale with a commission to Sussex Contemporary; there is no hanging fee, but delivery and collection are the artist's cost. The call opened in August 2026 and closes at 11:59pm on 21 February 2027, with artists notified in the week of 8 March and drop-off on 12 April. — Deadline: February 21, 2027. Fee: £20 per work (up to 3). Prize: Exhibition at Fabrica + Mentoring prize.

item.title: ZONE 6 — Collective Photobook Open Call · Zone Magazine
item.description: ZONE is an independent book publisher and photography-based visual arts platform started in 2018 and run by its founder Ali Beşikçi as a one-person operation; this is the open call for its sixth collective book, after five earlier volumes that between them published more than 650 artists from around the world. There is deliberately no theme. The interest is in what happens when images from different contexts are placed together and begin to act like parts of a larger organism, so the call is open worldwide to all visual arts - photography first, but also painting, illustration, sculpture, design, film stills, anything printable in a book - with no restriction on age, accomplishments or approach. You may send images from one or more projects; they are considered individually, and selection is said to rest solely on the images, not on CV or status, with a stated preference for giving visibility to lesser-known artists. Selected artists are published in the sixth collective book in offset print, with print run, size and design decided by the character of the work; the curator selects, edits and sequences the images and places them alongside other works, but will not crop or alter them without consent. Favourite works are also shared on ZONE's social channels during and after the call, whether or not they make the book. Selected artists do not receive a free copy but may buy any number at 50% off. There are two ways to enter: pay a €10 submission fee for up to 10 images, or pre-order the book at the early-bird price of €30, which includes one submission of up to 10 images; both are non-refundable and neither guarantees inclusion, and every additional submission needs its own fee or pre-order. Payment through the page redirects to an upload form; files are JPEGs under 2 MB named First Last Number.jpg, with your Instagram username in the message, and submissions that ignore the naming rules may be excluded without refund. High-resolution files are requested only if selected.
