Deadline 30 November 2026; featured artists are announced on 1 February 2027 on the website, social media and newsletter, and the book is due in spring 2027. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: €10 (up to 10 images) or €30 book pre-order incl. submission. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Germaine Van Parys Award 2026
item.description: Named for Belgium's first female photojournalist, who made her debut at Le Soir in 1918 and founded the Van Parys agency in 1956, the Germaine Van Parys Award is a Brussels-based programme for women photographers working in a documentary approach, organised by the non-profit Out of Focus and now in its third edition after laureates in 2024 and 2025. The 2026 call runs from 15 September to 1 December 2026 and is open to women photographers of all ages and nationalities, including anyone who identifies as a woman; applications are free and may be written in French, Dutch or English. There are two categories. The Germaine Van Parys Award itself is a €8,000 production grant for a professional photographer - one whose work has previously been exhibited or published - to make an unpublished documentary project related to Brussels over ten months; the money is meant for production, travel, equipment, developing and digitising, while the organiser covers exhibition prints and framing for the show that follows. The Germaine Van Parys Mentorship selects five women photographers residing in Belgium for ten monthly in-person sessions in Brussels, held in French on the first Thursday of the month from February 2027, with a €1,000 grant each towards a project of their own choosing; applicants must be able to take part in French and commit to all ten dates. Both strands end with a Brussels exhibition in January 2028 - the award winner's finished work shown alongside a projection of the mentorship projects - and the award project is also published as a portfolio in Médor magazine. Applications go through a form on the website as a single PDF of no more than 10 MB: for the award, a CV of up to two pages, a short biography, 10 to 15 images and a project statement on the Brussels subject; for the mentorship, a CV, biography, 15 images, a project description and a motivation letter. One project per applicant. A jury of photography and visual-arts professionals will be published on the website; winners are announced on 21 December 2026 and must be available for a meeting on 7 January 2027. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €8,000 + 5 × €1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: River Margin — Water Bodies
item.description: Water Bodies is an online segment of River Margin, the ecology-and-botany journal founded in 2026 by Melbourne-based artist, musician and writer Lana Eileen, whose first issue is still assembling separately. This call is narrower and faster: work about bodies of water - rivers, streams, lakes, the ocean, wetlands and more - and about water's relationship to plants, animals and people, water histories and water stories, to be featured online. Photographers may send up to seven photographs, digital or film, as email attachments or through a Google Drive link (the journal asks entrants not to use WeTransfer, as the links expire before it can open them). The same call takes writing up to 10,000 words, sound art and music, film, and visual art; for visual art the journal accepts only painting, drawing, sculpture and traditional media, ruling out digital and AI-generated work - the no-AI rule is written under visual art, while photography is described simply as digital or film. Work must be in English but is welcome from anywhere in the world, and you may submit to more than one category as long as each follows its own rules; a short third-person bio and a link to your website or social media are helpful but not required. There is no fee and no payment: the journal says plainly that it is a volunteer-run project by one artist and cannot yet pay contributors, so the return is publication online. Submissions go by email with the subject Water Bodies Submission by 27 September 2026; because of the volume received, only successful entrants hear back, within two months of submitting, and the journal asks that nobody email to confirm receipt. — Deadline: September 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online publication.

item.title: Paralaje Magazine — No. 2: Fine Art Black & White
item.description: Paralaje is an independent contemporary photography magazine published in Spanish with English translation, in print and digital editions, directed and edited by George Riverón; its name borrows the astronomy term parallax for the idea that no image is absolute and everything changes with the point from which you look. After a first issue built from an open call, the second call is dedicated to black-and-white fine art photography: series in which light, shadow, form, the body, space, memory, intimacy or abstraction come together into a visual language of their own. The editors say they are not after a particular aesthetic or a closed definition of fine art, but want personal, coherent projects that can sustain a point of view across a series, and they will judge on the visual strength of the images, the coherence of the series and the distinctiveness of the approach. Any photographic process qualifies - digital, film, alternative processes or experimental techniques - and the call is open to photographers of any country, background, age or level of experience. A submission is a series of 4 to 8 black-and-white photographs with a title, a short statement, a short biography, city and country of residence, and a website or Instagram if you have one, sent through a Google Form linked from the call page. Selected series appear in Paralaje No. 2, dated October 2026, in both the print and digital editions, with the magazine reserving a final editorial pick of which images from each chosen series are printed. There is no submission fee, no payment or free copy is mentioned, and the deadline is 30 September 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication in print & digital.

item.title: Home Fires: 37th Annual Members' Show · Tulsa Artists' Coalition
item.description: The Tulsa Artists' Coalition is a volunteer-run non-profit gallery in the Tulsa Arts District that mounts around eleven exhibitions a year at no cost to the exhibiting artists; Home Fires is its 37th annual members' show, pitched as a celebration of Tulsa's art community and the bonds that make TAC a place to come home to. It is open to all media with no restriction on subject beyond hate speech, and it is a members' show in the buyable sense: new and renewing memberships are accepted up to and including the submission deadline, and membership runs from $35 for an individual ($15 for full-time students, $50 per household), so a photographer anywhere can enter by joining, though accepted work must be delivered to the gallery on 26-27 December 2026 and unsold work collected on 23-24 January 2027. Members may submit up to two original pieces made in the last two years, one form per piece, as JPEGs of at least 1,200 pixels on the long side; because of the gallery's size only one piece per artist is selected, and work may be no larger than 24 inches on its longest side and must arrive ready to hang. Selection is from the digital submissions by a Selections Committee of three jurors - artists, educators and other art professionals, changed every year - with accepted and declined artists emailed by 5 December 2026. The show runs 1-23 January 2027 with the opening at the First Friday Art Crawl on 1 January, where a Grand Prize and three juror's choice cash awards are announced; the amounts are not published. Submissions opened 8 September and close at midnight Central time on 7 November 2026 through the coalition's Submittable portal, where the entry form carries no fee. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: Free (TAC membership required; from $35, students $15). Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Kerkini Wetlands Photo Award 2026
item.description: A new annual international photography award dedicated to Lake Kerkini in Northern Greece, a Ramsar-listed wetland with more than 300 bird species and, in the organiser's words, one of Europe's premier destinations for wildlife and bird photography. The 2026 edition is the first, organised by Agkistro Action, a social cooperative in the Serres region, and it is built as a conservation platform rather than a tourism promotion: the stated aim is to build a lasting visual archive of the lake and to promote environmental awareness through photography. Four categories - Birds of Kerkini, Wildlife of the Wetland, Wetland Landscape, and Human & Wetland - and the one hard rule is geographic: every photograph must have been taken within Lake Kerkini National Park or its surrounding wetland ecosystem, though there is no restriction on when it was taken, so archive work from earlier visits qualifies. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide aged 18 and over; entrants aged 18 to 25 are automatically considered for the Young Photographer of the Year Award. The entry fee is €15 per participant for up to 10 photographs across one or more categories, submitted as JPEGs through Picter. The prize fund is €3,000: €1,000 for Photo of the Year, €400 for each of the four category winners, and €400 for the Young Photographer award, plus trophies, up to five special mentions, and a place in the official exhibition for winning and shortlisted work. The jury is Costas Vidakis, Ellie Rothnie, Emil Enchev and Nikos Petrou, judging anonymously. The rules run to a detailed ethical-wildlife code (no baiting, no captive animals, no sky replacement or compositing) and ban images generated or altered with AI, while AI-based noise reduction and sharpening are allowed. Photographers keep copyright and grant only a non-exclusive, non-commercial, credited licence tied to the award. Submissions run 20 September to 20 November 2026; finalists are announced on 5 January 2027 and winners at the awards ceremony on World Wetlands Day, 2 February 2027. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: €15. Prize: €3,000 in prizes + Exhibition.

item.title: Call for Artists: 2027 Exhibition Season · Red Brick Center for the Arts
item.description: The Red Brick Center for the Arts, the City of Aspen's arts centre, invites artists living and working in Colorado to apply for its 2027 exhibition season. The programme runs solo exhibitions in the West Gallery and curated group exhibitions in the Main Gallery, and artists selected through this call are considered for the four 2027 slots: 11 February to 26 March, 10 June to 31 July, 12 August to 15 October, and 2 December 2027 to 10 January 2028. There is no fee to apply. The Gallery Committee reviews submissions and recommends artists whose work, in the centre's words, demonstrates artistic excellence, originality, and meaningful engagement with contemporary ideas and practices; the Red Brick's recent programme includes the 2025 Colorado Juried Exhibition and a solo show by the photographer Wendi Schneider. Photography is named outright in the accepted media, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, ceramics, textiles, sculpture, mixed media and experimental work, and proposed work must not have been exhibited at the Red Brick before. Applicants submit an artist statement and biography, 8 to 12 images of recent work labelled with title, dimensions and medium, and a 250 to 500 word exhibition proposal describing the themes, any new work planned for 2027, and how it relates to the wider practice; a CV and website are optional. Artists are responsible for delivery and return shipping; work is offered for sale during the show with a 60/40 split in the artist's favour, and the exhibition agreement asks that photographs and other paper works be framed under glass or Plexiglas unless another presentation is agreed. Applications close 30 September 2026 and artists are notified on 6 November 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: TAC Gallery 2027 Exhibition Submissions · Tulsa Artists' Coalition
item.description: The Tulsa Artists' Coalition, a 501(c)(3) that runs TAC Gallery in the Tulsa Arts District, is taking proposals for its 2027 exhibition season. The gallery at 9 East Reconciliation Way mounts a new exhibition every calendar month, and artists may propose a solo show, a collaboration with other artists, or a themed group show they would curate. Submissions in all media and disciplines are eligible, subject to the physical constraints of the space - two 24-foot main walls that take work up to 11 feet high - with an emphasis on the contemporary perspective and a body of work with a consistent style or theme. Work should have been completed within the last several years (unless a retrospective) and not shown in Tulsa in the last two years. Read the geography before applying: the Coalition's mission is to support artists in Tulsa and the surrounding area, so out-of-area proposals are accepted but capped at two per eleven-month season, and artists living in Tulsa temporarily, on a fellowship for instance, count as out of area. There is no submission fee. Applicants upload ten images or video with brief descriptions including media and dimensions, a statement of the proposed exhibit's theme, and a bio or resume, through Submittable. A Selections Committee of three jurors - artists, educators and other art professionals, changed each year - reviews the proposals and the 2027 schedule is settled by 15 November 2026. TAC provides installation help, a First Friday opening reception, press and social promotion, and volunteer gallery sitting, and has historically absorbed most exhibition costs; artists cover shipping both ways, provide statements and a price list, and TAC retains a 35% commission on sales (30% for members). The gallery carries no insurance on exhibited work. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.
